The natural questions are, if we expend more rounds, can we reduce the sample complexity? And how many rounds are needed to achieve the information-theoretic optimum of a linear query complexity? Many recent works have focused on this question without concern for the number of rounds expended (Ajtai et al., 2009; Daskalakis and Kamath, 2014; Suresh et al., 2014; Acharya et al., 2014, 2018a), culminating in algorithms with linear complexity. When the round complexity is analyzed, it can be shown that all these methods take O(log k) rounds. We state the implied results for our setting in the following claim, omitting details as we will shortly improve on the round complexity to be O(log log k).

The algorithm requires O(k) queries. 4.3. A Sub-Quadratic Algorithm with 2 Rounds In this section, we give a simple 2-round algorithm which results in a significantly better query complexity of O(k 4/3 ). In Appendix G, we generalize this to t-round protocols, but provide this as a warm-up and to convey one of the main ideas.
